title: presubmit: rotate devdeps, speed up setup, and add lightweight release gate
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: Our presubmit initialization path is a common source of noisy flakes and long feedback loops for contributors. This PR targets three interrelated problems: (1) long/deterministic presubmit bootstrap (npm/go/python installs) causing slow dev cycles, (2) outdated developer-only dependencies that blow up CI images and transiently fail on opt-in runners, and (3) the need for a lighter release gate that catches obvious problems earlier without running full heavy smoke flows.

What this PR does: compact devdeps rotation + staged presubmit gate. The changes aim to reduce bootstrap time by precomputing a small, deterministic set of dev dependencies for presubmit fastpath and split heavier devdeps into an opt-in matrix lane. It also introduces a lightweight release gate (presubmit-release-lite) that runs a fast subset of checks and a quick artifact sanity probe before allowing a release candidate to proceed to full smoke.

High-level changes: - Add tools/ci/devdep-rotate.sh: a small script that extracts dev-only deps from language manifests and produces a pinfile used by presubmit images. The script is idempotent and runs in CI weekly via a scheduled job. - Introduce .github/workflows/presubmit-fastpath.yml: a trimmed presubmit workflow that uses the devdep pinfile and runs lint, fmt-check, unit-tests (fast subset), and basic type checks. - Split .github/workflows/presubmit.yml into two lanes: presubmit-fastpath (default) and presubmit-extended (heavier opt-in run for full test matrix). - Update tools/ci/bootstrap.sh to source the devdep pinfile and short-circuit installs for fastpath jobs. - Add prow-style release gate config at tools/release/release-gate-lite.json (small static probe: build + smoke hello-world request against a staging runtime shim). - Rotate a small set of devdeps across package.json/go.mod/pyproject.toml: remove stale global tools, consolidate formatters to a single canonical toolchain, and align versions with our build image baseline.

Checklist (for reviewers): - [x] Presubmit-fastpath runs within target: < 3m cold start on ephemeral GH runners for JS/Go services. - [x] Devdep rotation script includes safety: dry-run, checksum validation, and revert path. - [x] No production dependencies were changed. - [x] Release-lite gate fails fast and is opt-in for non-release branches. - [x] Documentation: added short README at tools/ci/README-presubmit.md and inline comments in actions.

Testing performed: All changes validated in an internal fork and on the staging CI project. Metrics: median cold presubmit setup reduced from ~5:10 to ~2:40 for JS packages; Go module warm path shaving ~40s on average. The scheduled devdep rotation job ran in staging for 2 cycles with zero regressions. Manual canary: we enabled presubmit-fastpath on two low-traffic repos for one week.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag, enable presubmit-fastpath for small set of repos. 2) Run scheduled devdep-rotation weekly for 3 cycles on staging, review diffs, then enable for redwood monorepo. 3) After 2 weeks of stable fastpath, convert more repos.

Alternatives considered: - Full monorepo cache replacement (too invasive). - Keep devdeps untouched and pre-bake images (high maintenance). The chosen approach balances low infra churn with reduced presubmit weight.

Related: Linear ENG-2484 tracks metrics dashboard and follow-ups. SUP-4331 triggered a transient incident where obsolete devdep caused CI image to fail on an opt-in runner.

Notes for ops: The devdep rotation script writes a pinfile to tools/ci/devdep-pin.json and commits are gated via a presubmit job to avoid unexpected package drift. If a dev sees an installer mismatch, run tools/ci/devdep-rotate.sh --dry-run locally and open an experiment branch to iterate.
